text: On 29 January 2009 the police arrested a person who was protesting peacefully in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a reaction to the arrest of a peaceful protester in front of the Prosecutor General's Office on 29 January 2009, the applicant organisations decided to hold a demonstration in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a reaction to the arrest of a peaceful protester in front of the Prosecutor General's Office on 29 January 2009, the applicant organisations decided to hold a march from the Prosecutor General's Office to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a reaction to the arrest of a peaceful protester in front of the Prosecutor General's Office on 29 January 2009, the applicant organisations decided to hold a demonstration in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 2 February 2009 the first and the second applicants lodged a notification with the municipal authorities stating their intention to conduct a demonstration in front of the Prosecutor General's Office, followed by a march to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and a demonstration in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the notification lodged on 2 February 2009, the first and the second applicants described the planned event as a spontaneous reaction to the events of 29 January 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the notification lodged on 2 February 2009, the first and the second applicants relied on Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 2008.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 February 2009 the first and the second applicants organised a protest demonstration in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: From the video submitted by the parties, it appears that approximately twenty individuals took part in the demonstration on 3 February 2009 in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third applicant was among the participants in the demonstration on 3 February 2009 in front of the Prosecutor General's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Several minutes after the beginning of the demonstration on 3 February 2009, the protesters were attacked by six men wearing masks.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The six masked attackers physically assaulted the protesters during the demonstration on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The six masked attackers sprayed tear gas over the protesters during the demonstration on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The six masked attackers sprayed paint over the protesters during the demonstration on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a result of the attack on 3 February 2009, the third applicant sustained numerous injuries to his head and limbs.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a result of the attack on 3 February 2009, the third applicant needed medical treatment.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The protesters defended themselves and managed to chase away the attackers during the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The protesters managed to immobilise two of the six attackers during the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: One of the attackers admitted to having been paid 1,000 Moldovan lei (approximately 60 euros) by an unknown person for his participation in the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: From the very beginning of the gathering on 3 February 2009, four uniformed police officers observed the event from a patrol car parked close to the place of the event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The event on 3 February 2009 was filmed by approximately six people in plain clothes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicants, the approximately six people in plain clothes who filmed the event on 3 February 2009 were police officers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Government denied that the approximately six people in plain clothes who filmed the event on 3 February 2009 were police officers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the clash between the protesters and the attackers began on 3 February 2009, no police officer intervened.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The protesters called the police and requested assistance during the attack on 3 February 2009, but received no assistance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A police patrol appeared only one hour and a half after the attack began on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police patrol that arrived one hour and a half after the attack began on 3 February 2009 took the two immobilised attackers into custody.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The organisers of the demonstration lodged a criminal complaint with the Prosecutor General's Office following the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the criminal complaint lodged with the Prosecutor General's Office, the organisers of the demonstration complained inter alia about the failure of the police to intervene promptly during the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A criminal investigation was initiated following the criminal complaint lodged by the organisers of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: All six attackers who attacked the demonstration on 3 February 2009 were identified in the course of the criminal investigation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Only two of the six attackers were eventually given suspended sentences of four years for violation of the freedom of assembly of others and hooliganism.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: No action was taken in respect of the applicants' complaint about the inaction of the police during the attack on 3 February 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to Section 10 of the Assemblies Act of 2008, the organisers of a demonstration must notify the local authorities five days in advance about the planned demonstration.
Under Article 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 2008, no obligation to notify local authorities five days in advance exists for spontaneous demonstrations.
Under Article 12(5) of the Assemblies Act of 2008, no obligation to notify local authorities five days in advance exists for demonstrations with fewer than fifty participants.

According to Article 67 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the failure by organisers of a demonstration to notify the local authorities in accordance with the provisions of the Assemblies Act of 2008 is punishable with a fine of up to 800 Moldovan Lei.
The fine of up to 800 Moldovan Lei under Article 67 of the Code of Administrative Offences was the equivalent of approximately 50 euros at the time of the events.
